xBRIEFInfo.description: Story xBRIEF for #3708: offer the design-critique decision at Accept. Affordance only.

plan.title: feat(triage): offer the design-critique decision at Accept

narratives.Description: After a triage candidate is accepted, nothing offers the operator the design-critique decision. The judgment happens only when someone remembers it exists. This makes the choice available at the moment it becomes actionable: the accept verb names the command in its output, and the skill's post-Accept flow offers it as a choice. Declining writes nothing.
narratives.Overview: SCOPE WAS CORRECTED TWICE BY THE OPERATOR. This is an AFFORDANCE, not a checkpoint. An earlier revision described recording obligations, verb-level enforcement and ADR-005 ordering constraints, gated behind #3579; all of that is withdrawn. A single-critic arc ran against that superseded body and its close recommendation is moot -- the arc disposition comment on the issue records what survives. The #3702 arc-2 N=3 panel tested the checkpoint superset and refuted it; the affordance survives because the fatal findings were conditional on features this does not have.
narratives.UserStory: As an operator who has just accepted a triage candidate, I want the design-critique decision offered to me at that moment, so that running one is a choice I am given rather than a rule I have to remember.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Find where `triage:accept` builds its success output. Message construction is in `packages/core/src/triage/actions/index.ts` -- the accept path there emits `accept #<N> (<repo>) -> <decision_id>`. Add a line naming the design-critique command so the affordance appears without anyone remembering it. 2. Add the choice to the triage skill's post-Accept flow. THE SKILL IS GENERATED: the body lives in `content/packs/skills/skills-pack-0.1.json` (`"path": "skills/deft-directive-triage/SKILL.md"`). Edit the pack and render; editing SKILL.md directly will be overwritten. 3. Declining must write nothing -- no field, no label, no comment, no artifact. Not choosing it is just not choosing it. 4. Define behaviour under `triage:accept --auto-promote`, which collapses accept and promote into one action. 5. Regression coverage on the accept output line. 6. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] line.
narratives.LockedDecisions: AFFORDANCE ONLY. FORBIDDEN: any gate, any enforcement, any required question, any recorded negative, any new label, any new field, any title token, any verification step, and any dependency on another issue. Nothing may fail or block as a result of this change. `verify:judgment-gates --enforce` stays opt-in unused per the ADR-005 rollout. NOT the automated path -- #3579 and #3578 own auto-triage stamping and auto-dispatch; they are separate work, neither blocks nor is blocked by this, and #1423's state is irrelevant. If the operator DOES run a critique, the existing ADR-005 positive path (marker -> mirrored label -> clearance) is used unchanged and untouched. Two findings from the #3702 panel still apply: `accepted` does not mean `will be built`, so the offer must behave sensibly under --auto-promote; and ADR-005 governs the positive path only. SCOPE DISCIPLINE: this issue was over-built twice. If implementation starts requiring a new field, a new label, a verification step, or a dependency, that is scope drift, not a requirement.
narratives.AcceptanceJustification: Eight clauses from the recut issue checklist. Most are prohibitions, because the arc history shows this scope drifts upward under its own momentum.

intended_placement.cohesion_exemption: The skill pack and its rendered output carry the operator-facing half of the same affordance and must change together; CHANGELOG.md is outside any module boundary. Two paths were added to file_scope after implementation began, by the operator rather than the worker: `packages/cli/src/triage-actions.ts` is the only surface that prints the accept output, so the core formatter is unreachable without it, and `packages/core/src/content-contracts/skills/triage_skill.test.ts` is where skill body text is pinned. Both were an under-declaration in the original scope, not worker drift; the diff adds no capability beyond the declared affordance.
